definition: Small text files stored on your device by websites to remember information about your visit, such as login status, preferences, and browsing activity.
metaDescription: Learn about cookies - small files websites store on your device to remember your preferences, login status, and track your browsing activity.
simpleExplanation: Think of cookies like digital sticky notes that websites leave on your computer. When you visit a site, it might leave a note saying 'remember this person likes dark mode' or 'they're logged into their account.'
whyItMatters: Cookies can improve your browsing experience by remembering your preferences, but they can also track your behavior across websites for advertising purposes, raising privacy concerns about data collection.
technicalDetail: Cookies are HTTP headers sent by web servers and stored in your browser's local storage. They include attributes like expiration dates, domain scope, and security flags. First-party cookies come from the site you're visiting, while third-party cookies are set by external services like advertisers.

examples.explanation: When you add items to an online store's cart and return later, cookies remember what you selected so your cart isn't empty.
After logging into your email, a cookie keeps you signed in so you don't need to enter your password on every page.
Third-party cookies track which websites you visit to show targeted ads, like seeing shoe ads after browsing footwear sites.
